## Purpose and Entry Points
VoiceStudio is a local-first voice-production platform: voice cloning/design, TTS, dictation, video dubbing, long-form audiobooks, batch work, a local API, MCP, and optional remote workers. The primary desktop product is Electron; Tauri remains a sunset path. Backend server entry: `backend/main.py`; Electron main/renderer entry: `electron/src/main/index.ts`, `electron/src/renderer/src/main.tsx`. The Python OmniVoice model package also exposes CLI workflows under `omnivoice/cli/infer.py` and `omnivoice/cli/train.py`.

## Desktop Host and UI Boundary
Electron owns window lifecycle, backend bootstrap/download, privileged OS features, IPC, updater behavior, and trusted-renderer policy. Its renderer is a React/Vite workspace application organized around clone, dubbing, longform, dictation, gallery, settings, and tools. Renderer-to-backend traffic is mediated by API clients and event/WebSocket utilities rather than directly accessing Python internals.
Paths: `electron/src/main/backend.ts`, `electron/src/main/ipc.ts`, `electron/src/renderer/src/router.tsx`, `electron/src/renderer/src/lib/api/client.ts`.

## API and Application Orchestration
The Python backend is the control plane: FastAPI routers expose feature-specific HTTP, streaming, and WebSocket endpoints; core modules provide auth, configuration, persistence, events, task/job state, diagnostics, and filesystem safety. Routers delegate into services rather than invoking engines directly. Public integration surfaces include OpenAI-compatible APIs, the speech platform, and MCP.
Paths: `backend/main.py`, `backend/api/routers/generation.py`, `backend/api/routers/tts_stream.py`, `backend/api/routers/openai_compat.py`, `backend/mcp_server.py`.

## Synthesis and Model Runtime Layer
TTS requests flow through engine routing and the TTS backend/model lifecycle, which select compatible installed engines, enforce device/memory budgets, load/unload models, and isolate unstable dependencies in subprocess sidecars where needed. Supported engine implementations include bundled OmniVoice plus GGUF, IndexTTS, CosyVoice, PocketTTS, Supertonic, and others; model inventory is data-driven.
Paths: `backend/services/tts_backend.py`, `backend/services/engine_routing.py`, `backend/services/model_manager.py`, `backend/config/models.yaml`, `backend/engines/omnivoice_gguf/backend.py`.

## Media Production Pipelines
Dubbing is a staged asynchronous workflow: ingest media/subtitles, ASR and diarization/segmentation, translation, speaker/voice assignment, timed synthesis and fitting, QC, then audio/video/subtitle export. Long-form rendering similarly parses/imports scripts, plans segmented jobs, synthesizes and resumes work, and renders audiobook outputs. FFmpeg is an important external binary boundary for media decode, muxing, and retiming.
Paths: `backend/services/dub_pipeline.py`, `backend/services/fit_planner.py`, `backend/services/longform_render.py`, `backend/services/ffmpeg_utils.py`, `backend/api/routers/dub_export.py`.

## Persistence, Jobs, and Realtime State
SQLite-style schema migrations and backend stores persist settings, profiles, projects, histories, and remote-worker state. Job queues/stores separate durable work state from request handling; the event bus distributes progress/status to streaming UI clients. Voice profiles and persona bundles are reusable assets crossing clone, design, dubbing, and long-form workflows.
Paths: `backend/core/db.py`, `backend/core/job_queue.py`, `backend/core/job_store.py`, `backend/core/event_bus.py`, `backend/migrations/versions/0010_remote_worker_schema.py`.

## Distributed and External Integrations
Local operation is default, with optional Hugging Face model retrieval/mirrors, configurable LLM and translation providers, outbound HTTP, Tailscale/network sharing, and remote GPU workers. Remote workers communicate through a versioned protobuf/gRPC-like protocol and have explicit capability, capacity, routing, deadline, TLS, and artifact-transfer boundaries. Docker deployment is available alongside packaged desktop runtimes.
Paths: `backend/worker/protocol/worker_v1.proto`, `backend/worker/scheduler.py`, `backend/worker/transport/server.py`, `backend/services/llm_providers.py`, `deploy/docker-compose.yml`.
